transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been making these little careless mistakes that are starting to bother me. Like I’ll write the wrong time down on a senior-center class sheet, or I’ll measure a board and still cut it just a bit short because I missed some small print. It’s not huge stuff, but it keeps happening enough that I thought I should come in.
Do you remember the correct information at the time, but somehow write or do the wrong thing anyway?

Yeah, that’s pretty much it. I’ll think I’ve got it right, and then I’ll look later and see I wrote the wrong time on the class sheet. Or I’ll measure a board, feel sure about it, and still cut it just a little short because I missed some small print. It’s little mistakes like that.
Do you feel like you're paying attention when you're making these mistakes?

I feel like I am paying attention, at least at the time. That’s what’s frustrating. I’ll look at the class sheet and still write the wrong time, or I’ll measure the board and think I’ve got it, but then I realize I skipped over some small print and cut it just a hair short. It’s little stuff, but I’m not trying to rush through it.
Do you often forget things that happened recently?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a lot of forgetting recent things, at least not in a way that stands out to me.
Do you have trouble remembering things from one day to the next?
I don’t think so, not in any clear way. I mean, I might have to think a second, but I haven’t really noticed trouble remembering things from one day to the next.
Have you noticed any difficulty learning new information?
I haven’t really noticed a problem learning new things. I mean, it might take me a little time like anybody else, but nothing that seems out of the ordinary to me.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried lately?
Not really, no. I mean, I have normal worries here and there, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling especially anxious lately.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
No, I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling sad or down lately. Just kind of normal ups and downs, but nothing that’s been sticking around.
Do you have trouble planning or organizing tasks and activities?

Yeah, a little. If I’ve got a few errands to run, or I’m trying to get ready for a workshop and I also have an appointment that day, I have a hard time putting it all in order. I’ll start one thing, stop and switch to something else, and then I’m rushing around at the end.
Do you find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish speaking?
I don’t think so, not in any major way. I might jump in once in a while like anyone does, but I haven’t really noticed myself cutting people off or blurting things out a lot.
Have you had trouble controlling your emotions when something frustrating happens?
Not really, no. I mean, I can get annoyed if something doesn’t go right, but I don’t think I lose control of my emotions or have big outbursts. It usually passes.
Do you ever feel like your mind is foggy or cloudy, making it hard to think clearly?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think of it as foggy or cloudy, exactly. Sometimes I’m just slower to get going mentally, but I haven’t noticed a clear “brain fog” feeling.
Do you often feel mentally tired or exhausted after performing tasks that require a lot of concentration?
I’m not sure I’d say often. If I really have to focus on something for a while, I might feel worn out afterward, but I haven’t noticed it as a big or regular problem.
Do you ever find it hard to find the right words when you're trying to express your thoughts or have conversations?
Not really, no. I might pause sometimes to think of a word, but I don’t feel like it’s a regular problem in conversations.
Do you have trouble staying focused on what you're doing?

Yes, sometimes. Like at the senior center, if I’m filling something out or working on building something, and people start talking at the next table or my phone lights up, my attention goes right over there. Then I have to stop and figure out where I left off.
Do you find yourself acting on impulse without thinking through the consequences?
I don’t think so, not in any serious way. I mean, I might say something quickly once in a while, but I don’t usually feel like I’m doing things without thinking about what could happen.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened in the past, like important events from your life?
No, I don’t think so. I can usually remember the main things from my past, especially important events. I might forget little details here and there, but nothing that feels unusual to me.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like headaches or muscle tension when you're making these mistakes or feeling frustrated?
Not really, no. I might get annoyed with myself when I make a mistake, but I haven’t noticed headaches or muscle tightness coming with it.
Do you often catch yourself making mistakes just as you're making them, or only later when you're reviewing what you've done?

Usually I don’t catch it right in the moment. It’s more often later, when I look back over it or somebody points it out. Like I’ll write the wrong time on a senior-center class sheet, or I’ll measure a board and still cut it just a little short because I missed the small print. It’s small stuff, but it keeps happening.
Have you noticed a decline in your ability to perform daily tasks compared to a few years ago?

A little, yes. I can still do my regular daily things, but the mix-ups have affected what I take on. I’ve stepped back from helping lead a couple of DIY workshops because I don’t want my mistakes to mess things up. And my wife has started double-checking plans so I don’t throw off family visits or activities at the center.
